title: Who Gets the Food? Who Shares It?

scenes.visual: a tube with two kinds of paramecium, alone then together, one shrinks; then the question
scenes.tts: In 1934, a scientist named Gowse published his counts of two kinds of paramecium grown in one tube. Paramecia are tiny one-celled living things that swim in water. They ate bacteria. Each kind grew well alone. Together, one kind stayed common, and the other shrank to a small number. Here is the question. Why do some living things fight over food, while others share it?

scenes.visual: matter and energy, food to animal; two animals one food; five needs; territory box
scenes.tts: Every living thing needs matter and energy. Animals get both from food. Competition happens when living things need the same resource, and there is not enough for all. Animals compete for food, water, shelter, territory and mates. Territory is the area an animal keeps others out of.

scenes.visual: quiet competition in the tube, population, robins, plants
scenes.tts: Competition is often quiet. Nobody has to fight. The paramecia ate the same bacteria. Bacteria eaten by one kind were gone for the other. A population is all the members of one species living in one area. Members of a population often compete, like robins hunting worms on one lawn. Plants compete too, for light, water and minerals.

scenes.visual: honeybee colony, jobs, food passed bee to bee, unequal shares
scenes.tts: Living things can also cooperate. Cooperation is when members of a population work together to meet their needs. A honeybee colony can hold tens of thousands of bees. Workers do different jobs, like caring for young and guarding the hive. They pass liquid food from bee to bee. The shares are not always equal.

scenes.visual: limiting factors biotic and abiotic; rabbits and foxes
scenes.tts: A limiting factor is anything in the environment that limits how many of a species can live in a place. A biotic factor is a living part, like food or disease. An abiotic factor is a nonliving part, like water or temperature. A community is all the populations in an area that interact. If a disease killed many rabbits, foxes that eat rabbits would find less food.

scenes.visual: three rows: compete, cooperate, limiting factors
scenes.tts: So why do some living things fight over food, while others share it? Some compete for the same limited resource, often without any fight. Others cooperate. And limiting factors, living and nonliving, set how many can live in a place.
